question: What is the primary protein that makes up human hair?
explanation: Hair is built primarily from a tough, fibrous structural protein known as keratin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the correct first step when inspecting a patient's scalp?

options.A: Comb the hair vigorously to remove loose strands
options.B: Apply a medicated shampoo to check for lather
options.C: Part the hair in multiple areas to view the skin
options.D: Shave a small patch to inspect the follicle roots

explanation: To properly check scalp health, gently part the hair in different spots so you can clearly see the skin underneath for any issues. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: A patient has patchy hair loss and scalp tenderness from wearing tight braids for months. What is the likely cause?
explanation: Constant pulling on the hair roots from tight hairstyles damages them over time, leading to hair loss known as traction alopecia. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which part of your hand should you use to massage a patient's scalp during a shampoo?
explanation: Always use the pads of your fingers! It cleans effectively while keeping your fingernails from scratching the patient's sensitive scalp. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why is it so important to rinse the hair thoroughly after shampooing?

options.A: Leftover soap residue can cause scalp irritation and dryness
options.B: Unrinsed shampoo actively accelerates hair follicle growth
options.C: Remaining soap prevents the hair from absorbing water
options.D: Residue permanently changes the natural color of the hair

explanation: Leaving soap behind can dry out the skin and make the scalp itchy and flaky. A good rinse keeps your patient comfortable! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why do tightly coiled hair textures often tend to feel drier than straight hair?

options.A: The scalp produces significantly less sebum in these individuals
options.B: Frequent washing strips away the natural protective proteins
options.C: Curly hair follicles lack sebaceous glands entirely
options.D: Natural scalp oils have trouble traveling down the curved hair shaft

explanation: Because of the bends and turns in coils and curls, the natural oils from the scalp have a harder time sliding down the full length of the hair. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: A bedridden patient has severely matted hair after weeks of illness. What should you do first?

options.A: Ignore the matting until the patient is fully discharged from the hospital
options.B: Wash the hair with a harsh clarifying shampoo to break apart the tangles
options.C: Cut the matted sections off immediately to save time during the bed bath
options.D: Apply a conditioner or detangling spray and work through small sections with a wide-toothed comb

explanation: Always respect your patient's dignity. Working gently with a lubricant and a wide-toothed comb avoids painful pulling and protects their personal autonomy. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: What are the tiny eggs of head lice that attach firmly to the hair shaft called?
explanation: Nits are the tiny, oval eggs that head lice cement securely onto individual strands of hair. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why do fungal scalp infections like ringworm (tinea capitis) usually need oral medication instead of just medicated shampoo?

options.A: Shampoos cannot easily penetrate deep into the hair follicle where the fungus lives
options.B: Oral medications are cheaper and easier for hospitalized patients to swallow
options.C: Medicated shampoos will permanently damage the texture of the hair shaft
options.D: Fungal infections on the head are completely unaffected by topical treatments

explanation: Washing the surface isn't always enough because the fungus digs deep inside the hair follicle where shampoos can't easily reach. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: Which detail is most important to include in your notes when charting routine hair care?

options.A: The exact minute the hair drying process started
options.B: Condition of the scalp and any abnormal findings
options.C: The total cost of the hair care products used
options.D: The exact brand of shampoo preferred by the nurse

explanation: Always focus your documentation on clear clinical facts, such as how the scalp looks and any unusual signs you spot. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of teaching a family home care after treating a patient for head lice?

options.A: To prove that the nursing staff performed their duties correctly
options.B: To prevent reinfection and spread among household members
options.C: To force the family to cut their hair short for safety
options.D: To ensure the patient buys the most expensive commercial products

explanation: Good teaching helps families clean bedding and check everyone else, stopping the lice from spreading right back to the patient! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)
